reason: No measured rollback depth justifies destructive default eviction of historical publications, and a generation count would not bound their physical bytes across durable evidence pins, caller leases, shared atoms, and independent database/filesystem owners. The adjacent proof-bundle owner remains under its existing configured lifecycle; this selection does not override it or justify unbounded job or Investigation/Workbench growth. Any new lifecycle or retention policy requires a separate decision.
escape_hatch: monitor and expand or relocate server.data_dir
take a verified backup before a supported repository removal
supported repository removal reclaims derived files and makes non-quarantined unpinned evidence sweepable; pins and retention-quarantined evidence remain
retention-quarantined evidence has no supported deletion procedure in this release and requires a separately reviewed administrator resolution

definitions.meaning: a published exact repository/commit/unit/domain scope that is not the live current scope
any store-accepted evidence_pin retention owner, including proof, checkpoint, and Investigation state, restored with the database
a process-local caller-publication lifetime guard, not a durable history pin

owners.name: evidence_publications
owners.retention: historical published and pinned superseded runs are unbounded; quarantined runs require administrator resolution; sweep-eligible backlog remains until bounded maintenance drains it
owners.protection: live current scope, every durable evidence pin, and retention quarantine
owners.backup_restore: database export and restore retain runs, associations, assertions, atoms, and pins
owners.count_metric: aggregate physical extraction-run, association, assertion, and distinct shared-atom rows; v1 does not compute or expose lifecycle partitions

owners.name: extraction_attempts
owners.protection: attempt history for exact extraction scopes
owners.backup_restore: database export and restore retain attempts

owners.name: extraction_outcomes
owners.backup_restore: database export imports outcomes; restore selectively clears candidate-control outcomes with candidate authority
owners.count_metric: aggregate outcome rows; v1 does not expose disposition partitions
owners.byte_metric: logical encoded receipt bytes; physical database attribution unavailable

owners.name: evidence_pins
owners.retention: pin rows follow their owning existing lifecycle rather than an intrinsic global policy; proof pins accumulate while proof retention is disabled and a positive proof TTL releases only its exact namespace
owners.protection: proof, checkpoint, Investigation, and any other store-accepted owner lifecycle
owners.backup_restore: database export and restore retain every pin kind
owners.count_metric: pin rows partitioned only into proof-bundle, investigation-artifact, and other exact kind-prefix components; v1 does not report distinct pinned-run totals

owners.name: proof_bundles
owners.retention: proof_bundles.retention defaults to disabled (empty or 0), so bundles accumulate; a positive TTL expires from latest successful materialization through the existing sweeper, which deletes the expired bundle and exactly its proof-bundle:<bundle_id> evidence pins but no extraction evidence; the independent evidence sweep may later reclaim newly unpinned superseded evidence when otherwise eligible
owners.protection: immutable bundle identity until its configured lifecycle expires it
owners.backup_restore: database export and restore retain bundles and their pins
owners.count_metric: bundle rows only; exact proof pin rows remain separate under evidence_pins and v1 does not report referenced-run totals
owners.byte_metric: logical canonical content bytes; physical database attribution unavailable

owners.name: durable_job_history
owners.retention: pending coalescing bounds only one pending target slot; claim releases that slot, and done, failed, and canceled rows have no deletion or pruning path
owners.protection: pending and active queue correctness; terminal history has no separately selected retention policy
owners.backup_restore: database export and restore retain job rows; startup legacy reconciliation currently reads all eight tables
owners.count_metric: aggregate rows partitioned only by exact table; v1 does not expose job-status partitions

owners.name: investigation_workbench_rows
owners.retention: semantic history and current projections have no aggregate or runtime-wired sweep; the package-local single-artifact sweep has no production caller and does not bound the other component tables
owners.protection: Investigation, Workbench, artifact-owner, review, dossier, authorization, and watch lifecycles
owners.backup_restore: database export and restore retain all component rows
owners.count_metric: aggregate rows partitioned only by all 24 exact component tables; v1 does not expose owner lifecycle partitions and investigation_run_job remains under durable_job_history

owners.name: candidate_artifacts
owners.retention: one current authority; failed partial generation residue can accumulate until a later successful cleanup or repository removal
owners.protection: current store pointer; incomplete residue has no authority
owners.count_metric: current and noncurrent managed manifest/member identities

owners.name: focused_indexes
owners.protection: current manifest and process-local reader references
owners.backup_restore: validated marker-free physical focused publications may be archived; restore re-fences authority and whole indexes otherwise rebuild

owners.name: resolver_catalogs
owners.retention: current replacement transition plus package-owned stages and residue; lifecycle inventories refuse at their operational scan bound
owners.backup_restore: validated marker-free physical publications may be archived, then authority is cleared and re-fenced
owners.count_metric: all package-owned installation-root entries and apparent bytes, with per-repository current manifest/member identities reported separately
owners.byte_metric: current canonical member bytes and all package-owned apparent file bytes reported separately

owners.name: caller_rows
owners.retention: admissions and outcomes are unbounded across generations
owners.protection: current generation and latest live-generation terminal diagnostics
owners.backup_restore: database export contains rows, but restore deliberately clears caller pointers, admissions, and outcomes
owners.count_metric: generation publications, admissions, and pair outcomes
owners.byte_metric: canonical bytes from successful receipts where available

owners.name: caller_artifacts
owners.retention: successful incomplete-generation residue is unbounded until directory capacity refuses new work
owners.protection: current complete publication and active process-local leases
owners.backup_restore: only validated unambiguous marker-free complete bytes may be archived; historical coverage is not promised, incomplete residue is omitted, and restore clears authority
owners.byte_metric: canonical receipt bytes and apparent file bytes

proof_bundle_retention_control.positive_lifetime_effect: deletes the expired bundle and exactly its proof-bundle:<bundle_id> evidence pins but no extraction evidence; the independent evidence sweep may later reclaim newly unpinned superseded evidence when otherwise eligible

derived_collection.canonical_metadata_metric: resolver and caller canonical byte metrics require a supported rooted nonblocking regular-file opener and are otherwise unavailable while physical inventory continues; lookup follows host path semantics, so byte-case aliases may validate canonical bytes on case-insensitive filesystems while exact-spelling physical inventory ignores them; metric kinds remain independent
derived_collection.data_volume_metric: filesystem total and available bytes for the verified data directory where a descriptor-bound capacity primitive is supported; otherwise unavailable; no used-byte or cross-kind total
